requirement: The system shall automatically escalate a support ticket when it has remained unresolved past its service-level agreement deadline.
The system shall compute a first response deadline for each new ticket based on priority and the customer's service tier.
The customer submits a support request via the portal; the system validates the request, creates a ticket and routes it to an appropriate queue.
The agent updates a ticket with a customer reply; the system records the message, updates the last activity time and resets the waiting-on-customer clock.
As a support agent, I want to see my assigned tickets in priority order so that I work on the most urgent cases first.
As a team lead, I want to reassign a ticket to another agent so that workload is balanced when someone is unavailable.
A ticket with the highest priority must be routed directly to the on-call engineer, bypassing the standard queue.
A ticket may only be closed when the agent has recorded a resolution summary and the customer has been notified of the outcome.
Every change to a ticket's status, assignee or priority must be recorded with the previous value, new value, actor and time.
The ticket table shall ensure that each ticket has a subject, a priority from the recognised set, and an opened time that is not in the future.
code:
-- support ticket table
CREATE TABLE ticket (
    ticket_id      BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    customer_id    VARCHAR(40)  NOT NULL,
    subject        VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    description    TEXT         NOT NULL,
    priority       VARCHAR(10)  NOT NULL,
    status         VARCHAR(20)  NOT NULL,
    queue_name     VARCHAR(40),
    assignee_id    VARCHAR(40),
    opened_at      TIMESTAMP    NOT NULL,
    last_activity  TIMESTAMP    NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT ticket_subject_not_blank CHECK (length(trim(subject)) > 0),
    CONSTRAINT ticket_priority_chk      CHECK (priority IN ('P1','P2','P3','P4')),
    CONSTRAINT ticket_status_chk        CHECK (status IN ('OPEN','ASSIGNED','AWAITING_REPLY','ESCALATED','RESOLVED','CLOSED')),
    CONSTRAINT ticket_opened_not_future CHECK (opened_at <= now())
);

CREATE INDEX ticket_assignee_idx ON ticket (assignee_id, status);
CREATE INDEX ticket_queue_idx    ON ticket (queue_name, status);
hard_negatives:
-- ticket message table
CREATE TABLE ticket_message (
    message_id    BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    ticket_id     BIGINT       NOT NULL,
    author_id     VARCHAR(40)  NOT NULL,
    body          TEXT         NOT NULL,
    is_internal   BOOLEAN      NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
    created_at    TIMESTAMP    NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT message_ticket_fk FOREIGN KEY (ticket_id) REFERENCES ticket(ticket_id),
    CONSTRAINT message_body_not_blank CHECK (length(trim(body)) > 0)
);
-- SLA target table
CREATE TABLE sla_target (
    target_id     BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    service_tier  VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
    priority      VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL,
    response_mins INTEGER     NOT NULL,
    resolve_mins  INTEGER     NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT sla_priority_chk CHECK (priority IN ('P1','P2','P3','P4')),
    CONSTRAINT sla_response_positive CHECK (response_mins > 0),
    CONSTRAINT sla_resolve_positive  CHECK (resolve_mins > 0),
    CONSTRAINT sla_tier_priority_unique UNIQUE (service_tier, priority)
);

requirement: Only the assigned agent, a team lead, or an administrator may change a ticket's priority; the customer must not be able to escalate their own priority.
The nightly support report shall list, for each queue, the number of open tickets, the median first response time and the SLA breach count for the previous day.
